description: Tidal-causeway islands accessible on foot or by vehicle at low water, but with critical safe-crossing windows that must be observed. Hand-curated. UKHO's tide-times APIs are not openly licensed; we link to the most authoritative free tide source for each. The UI renders these alongside or instead of ferry cards.

causeways.summary: Lindisfarne Causeway is a metalled road open at low water only. Crossing during the closed window has stranded vehicles every year — always check the published safe-crossing times for the day of travel.
causeways.safeCrossingWindow: Approximately 3 hours after high water until 2 hours before next high water (varies daily).
causeways.officialSourceLabel: Northumberland County Council - Holy Island safe crossing times
causeways.warning: Lindisfarne Causeway closes twice a day for several hours each tide cycle. Never attempt a crossing once water has reached the road.

causeways.summary: A cobbled granite causeway crosses the bay between Marazion and the Mount, walkable at low water only. Outside those windows the National Trust runs a small foot ferry from Marazion (extra charge).
causeways.safeCrossingWindow: Approximately 4 hours either side of low water; published daily by the National Trust.
causeways.officialSourceLabel: St Michael's Mount - getting here & tide times
causeways.warning: The causeway is slippery with seaweed; wear grippy footwear and do not attempt to cross with rising tide.

causeways.summary: A sandy causeway connects Bigbury-on-Sea to Burgh Island at low water. When the tide rises, a unique sea tractor (motorised platform on stilts) shuttles guests of Burgh Island Hotel and visitors to the Pilchard Inn.
causeways.safeCrossingWindow: Approximately 3 hours either side of low water on foot; sea tractor operates at high water.
causeways.officialSourceLabel: Burgh Island Hotel - sea tractor schedule
causeways.warning: Time your visit around tides; the sea tractor doesn't always run for non-residents.

causeways.summary: A natural shingle bar (the Dhorlin) emerges across the mouth of Campbeltown Loch at low water, allowing a 1 mile walk out to Davaar Island to see the cave painting of the Crucifixion.
causeways.safeCrossingWindow: Approximately 2 hours either side of low water. Do NOT attempt at neap tides or in poor weather.
causeways.warning: Tides rise rapidly here. Check Campbeltown tide times and allow a clear safety margin.

causeways.summary: A concrete causeway from Cramond village (Edinburgh) emerges at low water; safe-crossing times are posted on a yellow sign at the slipway.
causeways.safeCrossingWindow: Approximately 2 hours either side of low water.
causeways.officialSourceLabel: City of Edinburgh Council - Cramond Island crossing times
causeways.warning: Multiple visitors have to be rescued each year; always check the published times.

causeways.summary: Eilean Tioram ("the dry island") - on which Castle Tioram sits - is reached on foot across a tidal sand bar at low water from Doirlinn, Acharacle (Loch Moidart).
causeways.safeCrossingWindow: Approximately 3 hours either side of low water.
causeways.warning: Path floods rapidly with rising tide; do not linger past the published window.

causeways.summary: Several Scottish islands named Oronsay (or Oransay) are reached from a parent island at low water — most notably the Oronsay in the Inner Hebrides reached on foot from Colonsay across the Strand.
causeways.safeCrossingWindow: Approximately 3 hours either side of low water.
causeways.officialSourceLabel: Colonsay community site - Oronsay & The Strand
causeways.warning: The Strand is fully covered at high water; check Colonsay tide times.

causeways.summary: Permanent causeway built in 1991 — not strictly tidal but listed here as one of the recent road links that joined an inhabited Hebridean island to Barra.
Permanent road bridge from Kyle of Lochalsh to Kyleakin since 1995. The Glenelg-Kylerhea community ferry remains as the seasonal alternative.
Two permanent bridges connect Anglesey to mainland Wales: Telford's Menai Suspension Bridge (1826) and the Britannia Bridge (rebuilt 1980, A55 trunk road).
Hayling Island is connected to the South Coast mainland by a road bridge. A separate foot-ferry runs from West Beach to Eastney (Portsmouth).
